fixes.value: Two electrical wiring diagrams titled "Figure 1 Types of conductor". The top one, "3 Phase system – separate neutral and earth", shows a three-phase source with lines L1, L2, L3, N and E, a load, and dotted outlines: the L1 to L3 conductors are "circuit conductors (by definition)" and the conductors within the large dotted lines are "conductors in a system" since they are electrically connected to a common source of electrical energy. The bottom one, "System including both combined and separate neutral and earth conductors (single phase only shown)", shows L, N and a Protective conductor with a load; arrows mark "conductors in a system But not circuit conductors", and a note says the combined neutral/earth conductor is a circuit conductor as well as a conductor in a system.
